}}

{{recipe}}

'''Sweet pork condiment'''<ref>{{cite web|title=วิธีทำหมูหวาน|url=http://www.mythaimenu.com/วิธีทำหมูหวาน|work=mythaimenu|accessdate=30 September 2014}}</ref> (Thai: หมูหวาน) is a popular Thai food served with other kinds of foods such as chili paste, fried rice, and hot glutinous rice. It's very delicious.<ref name="thaifoodmaster">{{cite web|author=Hanuman|date=10 November 2010|title=Sweet Pork Condiment|url=http://www.thaifoodmaster.com/ingredient/meats/pork/1839|work=Thaifoodmaster|accessdate=30 September 2014}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] light [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 5 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]]
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
* 350 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (0.77 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] shoulder, neck, or belly

== Procedure ==

# Mix the light soy sauce and sugar together in a bowl. Add pork and [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] in the refrigerator for at least 36–48 hours, in order to maintain the quality and the taste of the pork.
# [[Cookbook:Steaming|Steam]] the pork over boiling water for about 20 minutes. After the steaming is finished, let the pork rest for about 10 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] the pork into pieces.
# Put the palm sugar into a pan, and stir it over a low heat until it melts. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until the sugar browns. Add fish sauce and water all together. 
# Add the pork to the sauce, and mix well to coat.
# Simmer the pork in the sauce for about 5–10 minutes, then mix the pork and the sauce together.
